title: Vaktboder
description: Anskaffelse av portable ballistiske vaktboder (minimum klasse BR6NS eller likeverdig) til beskyttelse av ambassader og andre sensitive lokasjoner i Oslo. Politiets fellestjenester (PFT) inngår på vegne av Oslo politidistrikt (OPD) en fireårig rammeavtale med én (1) leverandør om levering og installasjon av vaktboder, med tilhørende opplæring, vedlikehold og reservedeler. Rammeavtalen kan også benyttes av øvrige norske politidistrikter. Opsjoner omfatter bredere variant, større bod, vann og avløp, UPS eller batteribackup og alternativ RAL-farge, samt timepriser for montasjearbeid og service ut over garantitiden. Estimert behov er om lag tre (3) standard fullt utstyrte boder i avtaleperioden. Volumet er indikativt og ikke bindende. Anslått verdi er NOK 5 000 000 eks. mva. Rammeavtalens maksimale verdi er NOK 50 000 000 eks. mva. Tildeling etter beste forhold mellom pris og kvalitet, vektet med pris 40 prosent, miljø 30 prosent og kvalitet 30 prosent. Konkurransen gjennomføres på engelsk.

title: Kvalifikasjonsfasen - Anskaffelse av satellittbasert og optisk SAR (ny konkurranse)
description: Denne konkurransen erstatter tidligere kunngjort konkurranse 2026/2237 som ble avlyst 14.08.2026.Formålet med anskaffelsen er å supplere eksisterende overvåkingskapasitet med satellittbaserte, ikke-kooperative sensordata. Løsningen skal bidra til å styrke situasjonsforståelsen i norske havområder gjennom bruk av bildedannende sensorer (optiske og SAR – Synthetic Aperture Radar). Dette skal muliggjøre:verifikasjon av AIS-datadeteksjon av fartøy som ikke sender AIS (såkalte «dark vessels»)forbedret situasjonsforståelse og beslutningsstøtte i operative sammenhengerKystverket har prøvet ut bruk av ikke-kooperative sensordata fra satellitter sommeren og høsten 2025 gjennom selskapet Vake AS sitt presentasjon- oganalysesystem (vake.ai.). Utprøvingen av data i Vake baserte seg på optiske og SAR sensordata fra Sentinel-1 og 2 satellittene i EUs Copernicus-program og på AIS-data fra Kystverket.Kystverket ønsker å inngå avtale om tilgang til en allerede etablert og operativ løsning for satellittbasert deteksjon og analyse. Det er ikke aktuelt med utviklingsløp i denne anskaffelsen.Leverandøren skal dokumentere at den tilbudte løsningen var etablert og operativ ved tilbudsfristens utløp.Dokumentasjonen skal minimum bestå av:En teknisk beskrivelse av den tilbudte løsningen, herunder hovedfunksjonalitet, benyttede datakilder og sentrale analysefunksjoner.Skjermbilder som viser sentrale funksjoner i løsningen, herunder visualisering av satellittdata, objektdeteksjon og analysefunksjonalitet.Opplysning om dato for produksjonssetting av løsningen til kunde.Beskrivelse av løsningens operative anvendelse hos minst én kunde eller sluttbruker.Dokumentasjon som sannsynliggjør faktisk operativ drift før tilbudsfristens utløp, eksempelvis kundebekreftelse, driftsrapporter, oppetidsrapporter, brukerstatistikk eller tilsvarende.Avtalen vil ha en varighet på ett (1) år, med opsjon på forlengelse.

title: Liten lastebil - ca 5 tonn totalvekt

title: NRK 2026/673 Oppdragsavtale Sikkerhetsrådgivning og risikovurderinger for arbeid i områder med forhøyet risiko
description: Allmennkringkasteren Norsk rikskringkasting AS (NRK) sitt samfunnsoppdrag krever en risikoprofil som, særlig ved større internasjonale hendelser, skiller seg vesentlig fra tradisjonell næringsvirksomhet. Der de fleste virksomheter iverksetter sikkerhetstiltak for å unngå uforutsigbare hendelser, krever NRKs journalistiske mandat ofte at medarbeidere oppsøker konflikt, naturkatastrofer og politisk ustabile områder for å sikre den norske befolkningen tilstrekkelig og pålitelig informasjon til å delta i demokratiske diskusjoner. «Journalistens fotavtrykk» i et risikoområde er preget av utstrakt kildekontakt, eksponering i felt og behov for rask forflytning, noe som skaper unike sårbarheter som krever spesialisert sikkerhetsfaglig kompetanse.

title: Byrom i Haugesund - prekvalifisering for idékonkurranse
description: Konkurransen gjennomføres som en begrenset idékonkurranse i to trinn. Første trinn er en åpen prekvalifisering, hvor alle interesserte team kan søke om deltakelse. Oppdragsgiver tar sikte på å invitere åtte team til å levere anonyme løsningsforslag i konkurransens andre trinn.Haugesund kommune ønsker å hente frem sterke og fremtidsrettede ideer for videreutvikling av Haraldsgata med tilgrensende byrom og tverrgater. Det foreligger i dag ikke investeringsmidler for gjennomføring. Formålet med konkurransen er å få innspill til en helhetlig visjon for gågaten som på sikt kan realiseres etappevis gjennom kommunale budsjetter og aktuelle støtteordninger.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Frankfurter Rotkreuzkliniken VgV- Verfahren techn. Gebäudeausrüstung (HLSK) ALG 1-3,7, 8 - LPH 5-9
description: Die Frankfurter Rotkreuz-Kliniken e.V. beabsichtigen am Standort Klinik Rotes Kreuz in Frankfurt am Main die Funktionseinheit Zentral-OP um einen Operationssaal mit entsprechenden Nebenflächen sowie vorhandene zentrale Sterilgut-Versorgungsabteilung mit Nebenflächen zu erweitern. Projektiert ist der Anbau eines zweigeschossigen, nicht unterkellerten Gebäudes mit zentraler Lüftungstechnik auf einem begrünten Flachdach, sowie die Errichtung eines Erschließungsturm inkl. Aufzügen auf der Nordseite des Gebäudes. Dieser soll unter anderem die Erschließung des neuen Sterilgutflurs ermöglichen. Die Angliederung an das Bestandsgebäude erfolgt über einen kleinen Patio in unmittelbarer Verlängerung der bestehenden OP-Magistrale. Der bestehenden Aufwachraum, im südlichen Gebäudeteil verortet, wird um einen Isolierbereich mit zwei Bettplätzen erweitert. Im Erdgeschoss des Erweiterungsbaus sind Arztdiensträume mit eigenem Zugang verortet. Die Haupterschließung während der Baumaßnahme des neuen OP-Anbaus erfolgt über einen Verbindungsflur auf der Westseite des Bestandsgebäudes. Auf dem Klinikgelände werden weitere Baumaßnahmen realisiert. Die Gesamtkosten (KG100-600) für geplanten Erweiterungsmaßnahmen betragen ca. rund 15. Mio. € brutto. Für dieses Projekt werden Fördermittel eingesetzt. Die Arbeiten finden in städtebaulicher Enge sowie bei laufendem Krankenhausbetrieb statt. Der Zugang zum Baugelände im Innenhof des Klinikcampus ist über die Königswarterstraße gegeben. Inhalt dieser Ausschreibung sind die Leistungen der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung HLSK, der Anlagengruppen 1-3,7,8 gem. § 56 HOAI Detaillierte Hinweise sind der nachfolgenden Beschreibung zu entnehmen. Es handelt sich um ein Verhandlungsverfahren mit vorheriger Veröffentlichung eines Aufrufs zum Wettbewerb/Verhandlungsverfahren nach § 17 VgV. Zentrale Elemente des Verfahrens: Zweistufiges Verfahren: Der Angebotsphase ist ein Teilnahmewettbewerb vorgeschaltet. Welche Unterlagen wann vorzulegen sind, ergibt sich aus der Aufforderung zur Abgabe Teilnahmeantrag (Anlage- FRK-KRK 1.00_Aufforderung zur Abgabe Teilnahmeantrag).

Der bestehenden Aufwachraum, im südlichen Gebäudeteil verortet, wird um einen Isolierbereich mit zwei Bettplätzen erweitert. Im Erdgeschoss des Erweiterungsbaus sind Arztdiensträume mit eigenem Zugang verortet. Die Haupterschließung während der Baumaßnahme des neuen OP-Anbaus erfolgt über einen Verbindungsflur auf der Westseite des Bestandsgebäudes. Auf dem Klinikgelände werden weitere Baumaßnahmen realisiert. Die Gesamtkosten (KG100-600) für geplanten Erweiterungsmaßnahmen betragen ca. rund 15. Mio. € brutto. Für dieses Projekt werden Fördermittel eingesetzt. Die Arbeiten finden in städtebaulicher Enge sowie bei laufendem Krankenhausbetrieb statt. Der Zugang zum Baugelände im Innenhof des Klinikcampus ist über die Königswarterstraße gegeben. Inhalt dieser Ausschreibung sind die Leistungen der Objektplanung Gebäude und Innenräume nach § 34 HOAI, LPH 5-9. Detaillierte Hinweise sind der nachfolgenden Beschreibung zu entnehmen. title: Äidinmaidon pastörointilaite 1 + 1 optiolaite
description: Äidinmaidon pastörointilaite 1 + 1 optiolaite HUS-yhtymä pyytää tarjouksia äidinmaidon pastörointilaitteesta HUSin Äidinmaitokeskuksen käyttöön. Hankinnan kohteena on yksi (1) äidinmaidon pastörointilaite käyttöönotettuna sekä optiona yksi (1) vastaava laite. Laitteen käyttötarkoituksena on luovutetun äidinmaidon turvallinen pastörointi ja jäähdytys sairaalaympäristössä. Laitteen tulee soveltua äidinmaidon käsittelyyn, pastörointiin, jäähdyttämiseen sekä tarvittaessa pakastetun maidon sulattamiseen. Hankittavan laitteen tulee mahdollistaa pastörointiprosessin luotettava dokumentointi ja jäljitettävyys. Tavoitteena on hankkia käyttäjäystävällinen, toimintavarma ja hygieeninen ratkaisu, joka mahdollistaa äidinmaidon käsittelyn tehokkaasti sekä tukee potilas- ja käyttäjäturvallisuutta. Hankinnassa painotetaan erityisesti prosessin luotettavuutta, lämpötilanhallinnan tarkkuutta, tiedon tallennusta ja laitteen huollettavuutta. Hankintaan sisältyvät vähintään laitteen toimitus, asennus, käyttöönotto, käyttöönottokoulutus, käyttö- ja huoltodokumentaatio sekä takuuaikaiset palvelut tarjouspyynnön vaatimusten mukaisesti. Kyseessä on kokonaishankinta, eikä hankintaa ole jaettu osiin, koska toimitettavan kokonaisuuden tulee muodostaa teknisesti yhteensopiva ja käyttötarkoitukseensa soveltuva laitekokonaisuus yhdeltä toimittajalta. Optiona varataan oikeus hankkia yksi (1) vastaava laite vuosien 2026–2029 aikana. Tilaaja päättää option käyttämisestä erikseen. Optiolaitteen yksikköhinta on sama kuin tarjouksessa ilmoitettu laitteen yksikköhinta. Lisäksi tilaaja varaa oikeuden solmia hankittavalle laitteelle huolto- ja ylläpitosopimuksen takuuajan päättymisen jälkeen. Huoltosopimuksen tarkempi sisältö, laajuus ja kesto määritellään erikseen option käyttöönoton yhteydessä. Huoltosopimuksen hinnat huomioidaan tarjousten vertailussa, mutta tilaaja ei sitoudu huoltosopimuksen hankkimiseen. Hankinnan kohde ja sitä koskevat vaatimukset on kuvattu yksityiskohtaisesti tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä.,

title: North East London Community Dermatology Service
description: Market Engagement Event The proposed North East London (NEL) Community Dermatology Service will provide a consultant-managed service, aligned with British Association of Dermatologists (BAD) guidance, delivering specialist assessment, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up care for patients with skin, hair and nail conditions within community settings. The service will operate across Barking & Dagenham, Havering, Redbridge, Newham, Tower Hamlets and Waltham Forest, supporting timely access to care, improving patient experience and ensuring that patients receive treatment in the most appropriate setting. The service is expected to include referral assessment and triage, Advice & Guidance (A&G), specialist outpatient consultations, diagnostic investigations, minor dermatological procedures and the ongoing management of both acute and long-term dermatological conditions. The service will work collaboratively with primary care, acute trusts and other healthcare partners to provide integrated pathways of care and clear arrangements for onward referral where specialist hospital-based intervention is required. The model will focus on delivering high-quality, safe and effective care, improving equity of access across North East London, and making best use of community-based provision to meet population health needs. Market Engagement: To assist the Commissioners with testing its assumptions and proposed service requirements, a market engagement event will take place to explore the market's feedback on the following areas: • Outline of service requirements and key outcomes; • Timescales for procurement and mobilisation of the new contract; • Proposed contract duration and financial model; • Networking opportunity with providers. o Deadline to register: Wednesday 23 September 2026 at 12:00pm o Event: Tuesday 29 September 2026 from 12.00pm - 13.15pm Number of attendees: Maximum of 2 people per organisation. title: Belgium – Lift-maintenance services – Maintenance full omnium d'un parc multimarque d'ascenseurs, monte-charge et escalier mécanique et services associés
description: Le présent marché vise la maintenance d'un parc d’ascenseurs, monte-charge et escalier mécanique sur le site de l'aéroport de Liège. Il s'agit d’un parc multimarque : l’adjudicataire s’assure donc de pouvoir intervenir sur tout le parc, quelle que soit la marque, l’âge et l’état des installations. Les prestations visées concernent ce qui suit : • La maintenance préventive et curative, incluant les dépannages, en full omnium ; • Les prestations de modernisation règlementaires ayant lieu tous les 15 ans pour les ascenseurs concernés par la durée du marché ; • Des interventions éventuelles non couvertes par le full omnium. Le marché prend cours le lendemain de sa notification d’attribution et l’adjudicataire devra démarrer de manière opérationnelle le 1er avril 2028, date de fin du précédent contrat. Auparavant, après attribution du marché, l'adjudicataire aura notamment fait le nécessaire pour obtenir tous les accès aéroportuaires afin que son personnel puisse se rendre en zone airside sécurisée, éventuel(s) sous-traitant(s) compris. Le marché est lancé pour une période de 60 mois et pourra éventuellement être reconduit pour 3 périodes de 12 mois chacune sur décision de l’entité adjudicatrice communiquée par écrit à l’adjudicataire 3 mois avant la fin de la période en cours. Le parc est composé des éléments suivants : • 27 ascenseurs ; • 1 monte-charge ; • 1 escalier mécanique. Ces quantités pourront être revues à la baisse ou à la hausse en cours d'exécution en fonction de l'évolution du parc immobilier de l'entité adjudicatrice. Les dépannages doivent avoir lieu 7 jours sur 7 et 24 heures sur 24 selon dans les délais qui seront spécifiés dans le cahier spécial des charges. Un taux de disponibilité est imposé pour chaque équipement par an : 95% (les modalités seront précisées dans le cahier spécial des charges). Une visite de site sera organisée pour les candidats invités à remettre offre.

title: Schüchtermann-Klinik, Neubau Kardiologie Tischlerarbeiten - Innenwandbekleidung
description: Allgemein: Die Ausführung des fünften Bauabschnittes zum Neubau der Kardiologie der Schüchtermann-Klinik beinhaltet den Neubau des Gebäudeteils H als Erweiterung zum vorhandenen Gebäude. Die Schüchtermann-Klinik verbleibt während der gesamten Neubaumaßnahme in Betrieb, sodass hier erhöhte Anforderungen an den Emissionsschutz gestellt werden. Bei großflächiger Öffnung des vorhandenen Gebäudes sind ebenfalls die hauseigenen Hygienestandards zu beachten. Allgemeine Baubeschreibung: Bauteil H besteht aus einem L-förmigen Gebäudeflügel, der unmittelbar an ein in Funktion befindliches Krankenhausgebäude angrenzt. Der Gebäudeflügel besteht aus 2 Vollgeschossen (EG, 1. OG) und einem zurückgesetzten Staffelgeschoss (2. OG) sowie einem Untergeschoss. Baukonstruktion: Die tragenden und aussteifenden Bauteile einschließlich der Treppenhäuser und Aufzugsschächte werden aus Stahlbeton hergestellt. Die Deckenkonstruktion erfolgt in Massivbauweise. Tragende Wände bestehen aus Stahlbeton oder Kalksandstein. Nicht tragende Wände bestehen aus Trockenbau oder Kalksandstein. Zur Fassadengestaltung werden Einzelfenster aus Leichtmetallprofilen mit einer Verschattungsanlage verbaut. Zwischen den Fenstern sowie an den restlichen Fassadenflächen erfolgt eine Verkleidung aus Faserzementplatten. Auf den jeweiligen Etagen sind neben Akustikdecken, Gipsdecken, Metalldecken auch Putzflächen zur Ausführung vorgesehen. Die Bodenbeläge im Bereich der Treppenhäuser sollen aus Feinsteinzeug und in den übrigen Bereichen aus Polyvinylchlorid oder synthetischem Kautschuk bestehen.

title: Nelipyöräohjatun pienkuormaajan hankinta

title: Upgrading of the interpretation space at the Fonderie de l'Arsenal, Fortifications of Québec National Historic Site
description: 5P300-26-0115/A Upgrading of the interpretation space at the Fonderie de l'Arsenal, Fortifications of Québec National Historic Site BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA; YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsest-bidseast@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsest-bidseast@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-877-558-2349. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). This bid solicitation is issued in accordance with the conditions of Supply Arrangement No. 5P300-23-0156/A under Stream A. Only suppliers who are pre-qualified and have been issued a supply arrangement at the time this bid solicitation is issued are eligible to bid. Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency (PCA) requires a proposal to upgrade the interpretation space at the Arsenal foundry in Artillery Park, Fortifications of Québec National Historic Site. The Contractor must provide all the professional services required for the turnkey delivery of this project, from preliminary design to fabrication and installation, to transform the current temporary exhibit into a permanent, yet fully modular, interpretive facility. The scope of the project also includes a reflection on the interior design of the entire building as well as the turnkey development of certain exterior signage elements. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE The period of the Contract is from date of Contract to August 15, 2027 inclusive. BIDDERS’ CONFERENCE A bidders' conference will be held via teleconference on September 9, 2026. The conference will begin at 11:00 EDT. The scope of the requirement outlined in the bid solicitation will be reviewed during the conference and questions will be answered. It is recommended that bidders who intend to submit a bid attend or send a representative. Bidders are requested to communicate with the Contracting Authority before the conference to confirm attendance. Bidders should provide, in writing, to the Contracting Authority, the name(s) of the person(s) who will be attending and a list of issues they wish to table no later than September 7, 2026 at 2:00 PM. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the bidders' conference will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. Bidders who do not attend will not be precluded from submitting a bid. LANGUAGE REQUIREMENTS The Parks Canada Agency has an obligation to respect the spirit and letter of the Official Languages Act, R.S. 1985, c. 31 (4th Supp.). When representing the Crown, the consultant must therefore ensure that oral communications are in the preferred official language of the intervening participants. Written communications will be in the recipients' language(s) and must be forwarded to the Project Authority before being sent. If the intervening participants need to communicate with the consultant or its representatives by telephone, the consultant must ensure that all persons, including receptionists and other key people who receive these calls, are bilingual ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) calendar days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: Y1DZ--556-25-102 Green House Homes Steam (VA-26-00036216)
description: Contractor shall provide all tools, materials, labor, quality assurance, and supervision for renovations resulting in a complete, compliant, and fully-functional project as described throughout the contract documents � including the drawings and specifications. The purpose of this project is to provide steam service to Green House Homes 201 and 202. Existing gas fired hot water boilers (2 per home) and gas fired steam generators (1 per home) are to be replaced. Steam-to-Hot Water heat exchangers will replace gas fired hot water boilers and clean steam duct mounted humidifiers will replace exiting setup. Both homes are anticipated to be occupied during work. Construction will be phased to reduce impact on residents and FHCC operations, see sheet MS100. Removal and installation of duct mounted humidifier will be a one-day event (per home) due to AHU shutdown. All material will be required to be on site, and interior of ductwork immediately near installation will be clean and free of debris prior to AHU being returned to service.

title: Ireland – Laboratory services – Sampling and Analysis of Private Water Supplies in County Wexford
description: As the Supervisory authority for small private regulated water supplies in Wexford, Wexford County Council is required to monitor certain group water schemes and private premises which have their own wells, including caravan parks, schools, estates etc. The drinking water is sampled and analysed in accordance with S.l. No. 99/2023 - European Union (Drinking Water) Regulations 2023. Results are reported to Wexford County Council each month. The current compliance sampling contract ends on December 31st, 2026, and Wexford County Council is requesting tenders from interested parties for provision of these services. The service provider will be required to provide the following services: a) Compliance (and occasional investigative) sampling and analysis of drinking water for both 'check' and 'audit' parameters as set down by S.I. No. 99/2023 - European Union (Drinking Water) Regulations 2023 and listed in Appendix 1 Requirements and specifications. b) Occasional investigative sampling. These are normally duplicate samples i.e coliforms, e.coli free and total chlorine. Other parameters may also be asked for. c) In accordance with EPA requirements, all analysis of parameters in compliance samples (except for free and total chlorine, odour and taste and Dalapon) shall be accredited. Investigative samples do not have to be accredited. d) Reporting of results to Wexford County Council as detailed in Appendix 1 Requirements and specifications. There are currently about 170 private and group water supplies (Entities). This number is variable. It is expected that up to 15 additional schemes will be added during 2026 and these additional entities shall be sampled and analysed at tender rates. Each scheme shall have two check samples carried out annually. A small number of schemes will have more than two check samples and/or will require an audit sample. The level of analysis, including Limits of Detections must meet the requirements cited in S.I. No. 99/2023 - European Union (Drinking Water) Regulations 2023. The laboratory appointed (and/or sub contracted laboratory) must be accredited to !NAB (or equivalent) for all relevant parameters.

Lovell FHCC intends to issue an Invitation for Bid (IFB) for construction services to demolish and replace an existing 1000 ton York centrifugal chiller and associated systems. description: DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. This Sources Sought is a market research tool being used to determine potential and eligible business firms that are capable of providing the services described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a Request for Proposal. The existing contract was previously competed, with two offers received. Nevertheless, the Government would like to ensure that there is adequate competition for this procurement. Additionally, the results of this sources sought will also be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. All interested large and small businesses are encouraged to respond with a capability statement, but only those businesses or teaming arrangements that are considered small under NAICS 541330-1 will be considered for small business set-aside decisions. INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) at Patuxent River, MD announces its intention to procure, on a competitive basis services to provide Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Combat Systems, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (C6ISR) integration and installation; systems engineering support; In-Service Engineering Agent (ISEA); and logistics support to Mission Systems programs, systems, and technological areas within the SAIW project portfolio. Further details are provided in the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS)/Statement of Work (SOW) attached to this synopsis (Attachment 1). The services are currently being performed by The MIL Corporation of Bowie, MD under N00421-24-D-0002. The current contract is Cost-Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) containing both performance-based Completion CLINs and Level-of-Effort (LOE) CLINs. This contract is due to expire 14-FEB-2029. Although the current Period of Performance (PoP) of this requirement is scheduled to end Q2 FY2029, the estimated exhaustion date is now within Q1 FY2028. PROGRAM BACKGROUND As the organic Lead Systems Integrator� (oLSI�) for the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) operates under a product-based business model whereby NAWCAD WOLF civilians lead and manage the execution of the requirements with combined Government-Industry teams. Using this oLSI� approach, the Government maintains control of intellectual property and data rights, enabling WOLF to rapidly adapt solutions to the dynamic needs of the warfighter. The NAWCAD WOLF Ship & Air Integrated Warfare (SAIW) Division is the oLSI� providing design, procurement, integration, testing, and training of Command, Control, Communications, Computers, and Intelligence (C4I) electronic systems that meet the requirements of the United States Navy operating forces. The SAIW Division, operating under the oLSI� model, has requirements for services to provide Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Combat Systems, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance integration and installation (C6ISR); systems engineering support; In-Service Engineering Agent; and logistics support to Mission Systems programs, systems, and technological areas within the SAIW project portfolio. REQUIREMENTS Please review Attachment 1, Draft PWS/SOW and Attachment 2, Draft Hours. If your company has any questions about the PWS/SOW, Draft Hours, or any areas that may need further explanation, please also identify those in the response. The labor categories anticipated to execute the contemplated effort are included in Attachment 2, Draft Hours. Since the resultant contract will be a cost-type effort, the successful awardee will also be required to have a Government approved accounting system upon award. All Contractors that propose must either have or be able to obtain a TOP SECRET facility clearance. A DD Form 254 Contract Security Classification Specification shall apply to this requirement and the prime contractor shall have a �Top Secret� Facility Clearance and a �Secret� Safeguarding Clearance. ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this requirement is 541330-1 Engineering Services with a Small Business Size standard of $47 Million. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. The Product Service Code (PSC) for this effort will be K058: Modification of Equipment - Communication, Detection, and Coherent Radiation Equipment PLACE OF PERFORMANCE % On-Site Government % Off-Site Contractor WOLF St. Ingioes, MD 100% 22% 78% ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE The requirement is anticipated to be a Single Award, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA IDIQ) contract with Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) Level of Effort (LOE)/Term Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) for a portion of labor, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) CLINs for the remaining labor, and cost reimbursable CLINs for Other Direct Costs (ODCs). The proposed contract is anticipated to include tasking and labor categories that are subject to the Service Contract Act. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE It is anticipated that the resultant contract is estimated to begin in Q1 FY2028 and will have a five-year ordering period It is anticipated performance will commence approximately in December 2027. The estimated manhours hours by CLIN type are as follows: For the FFP CLINs: 272,910 manhours (for estimating purposes only, based on projections from historical data.) For the CPAF CLINs: 892,097 manhours SUBMITTAL INFORMATION It is requested that interested businesses submit to the contracting office a brief capabilities statement package (no more than 15 pages in length, single spaced, 12 point font minimum) demonstrating the ability to perform the effort listed in the attached Draft PWS/SOW, Attachment 1. This documentation must address, at a minimum, the following: Title of the PWS/SOW to which you are responding; Company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office location(s), CAGE code, DUNS number, and a statement regarding current small/large business status; Respondents to this notice must also indicate whether they qualify as a Small, Small Disadvantaged, Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Women-Owned, 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business (HUB) Zone, or Veteran Owned Small Business concern; If a small business, provide an explanation of your company's ability or your company�s ability combined with a similarly situated entity�s ability to perform at least 50% of the tasking described in this PWS/SOW; Resources available such as corporate management and currently employed personnel to be assigned to tasks under this effort to include professional qualifications, specific experience of such personnel, and the ability to have personnel located at the city specified; Management approach to staffing this effort with qualified personnel; Statement regarding capability to obtain the required industrial security clearances for personnel; Company's ability to meet the requirements in the Facility and Safeguarding requirements; Company's ability to begin performance upon contract award; Company's ability to manage a team of subcontractors, including a list of contracts and teaming arrangements; Prior/current corporate experience performing efforts of similar size and scope within the last three years, including contract number, organization supported, indication of whether as a prime or subcontract

title: Replace Perimeter Fence Pasture 7
description: IAW Attachment 1 - Statement of Work, The Livestock Arthropod Pest Research Unit (LAPRU) includes the Cattle Fever Tick Research Laboratory (CFTRL), which operates under biosecurity at the USDA Moore Air Base near Edinburg, Texas. This is a satellite facility of the Knipling-Bushland U.S. Livestock Insects Research Laboratory (KBUSLIRL) in Kerrville, Texas. Scientific endeavors at the CFTRL deliver technologies that the USDA Cattle Fever Tick Eradication Program can integrate to keep the U.S. free of cattle fever ticks in a sustainable manner. This ensures continued prosperity of the U.S. livestock industry. Unique assets at the CFTRL include cattle fever tick colonies, barns for studies with cattle that can be artificially infested with ticks, and pastures providing the ability to conduct studies with infested cattle resembling field conditions. However, modernization of the facilities is required to keep up with the expansion of the research program at the CFTRL that is underway to meet the expectations of the U.S. livestock industry and other stakeholders� groups. The current perimeter fence around pasture 7 is allowing wildlife onto the facility. This puts the facility at risk of losing our quarantine zones.

title: Residential Reentry Center (RRC) Services and Home Confinement Services Located within Bakersfield and surrounding areas within Kern county, California
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes located in Bakersfield, CA and the surrounding areas within Kern County, CA. This will be for a new expansion and not a replacement contract for current services. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for Home Confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work entitled, "Residential Reentry Center, March 2022 SOW�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, Programs, of the aforementioned SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be an indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity type contract with firm fixed unit prices for all line items. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a maximum of 25 beds in which 20 beds will be designated for males and 5 beds designated for females for the One-year Base Period and each of the Four One-year Option Periods The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a maximum of 15 placements to include both males and females for the One-year Base Period and each of the Four One-year Option Periods. The Home Confinement Radius will be within 150 miles of the RRC. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. 15BRRC26R00000022 will be available on or about September 23, 2026, and it will be distributed solely through the Government Point of Entry website at www.sam.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be available. The site provides downloading instructions. Future information about this acquisition will also be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure that they have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. The estimated closing date of 15BRRC26R00000022 will be on or about November 23, 2026. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by this agency. No collect calls will be accepted. No telephone request or written requests for the solicitation will be accepted.

description: ARCHITECT-ENGINEER INDEFINITE DELIVERY/INDEFINITE QUANTITY MULTIPLE AWARD TASK ORDER CONTRACT FOR GENERAL DESIGN AND OTHER RELATED SERVICES WITHIN THE BOUNDARIES OR ASSIGNMENTS OF MISSISSIPPI VALLEY DIVISION, UNITED STATES ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS Solicitation (Synopsis) Number: W912P826RA012 Set-Aside Code: Unrestricted with a Partial Small Business Set-Aside Product Service Code: C219 - Architect and Engineering - General North American Industrial Classification System Code: 541330 - Engineering Services 1. CONTRACT INFORMATION: These services are being procured in accordance with 40 United States Code, Chapter 11, Selection of Architects and Engineers Statute, Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 36. Firms will be selected for negotiation based on demonstrated competence and qualifications for the required work stated in this synopsis. This is not the Request for Proposal. Interested firms shall respond by submitting one Standard Form (SF) 330 listing their qualifications. North American Industrial Classification System Code is 541330, which has a size standard of $25,500,000 in average annual receipts. This Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) announcement is Unrestricted with a Partial Small Business Set-Aside pool. The resulting task orders will be negotiated Firm Fixed-Price for General Design and other related services. Multiple contract awards are anticipated, with a performance of five years, with four negotiated rate escalations each year after the initial first year. The total MATOC shared pool capacity shall not exceed $90,000,000 or five-year duration, whichever comes first. The minimum guarantee throughout the five-year contract is $1,000. Responding firms must address each evaluation criteria in the appropriate sections of the SF 330 for the prime contractor as well as all subcontractors and consultants. If subcontracted, clearly indicate what part of the scope they will be performing. To be eligible for the contract award, the firm must be registered in the Department of Defense (DoD) System for Award Management (SAM). Register via the SAM Internet site at https://www.sam.gov. For contractors requiring Common Access Cards (CAC) or contractors requiring unescorted access to USACE controlled property for greater than six (6) months the Centralized Suitability Service Center (CSSC) requires a T1 Background Investigation to be completed. Should a task order require a T1 Background Investigation it will be specified. The primary purpose of the proposed contract is to provide A-E General Design and other related Services anywhere within the boundaries or assignments of Mississippi Valley Division. 2. PROJECT INFORMATION: A-E and related services are to be accomplished through individual Task Orders, which shall consist of the following comprehensive scope tasks and requirements: (a) Core Engineering, Design, and Project Documentation: The work will involve investigations, comparisons, data evaluations, analyses, designs, water quality analyses, technical writing, and drafting for: Engineering Documents: Preparing Design Documentation Reports (DDRs) geotechnical reports, feasibility studies, plans and specifications, Operation, Maintenance, Repair, Replacement, and Rehabilitation (OMRR&R) manuals, value engineering, or other technical engineering documents. Design, Modeling & Drafting: Civil design, hydraulic design, hydrologicanalysis, sediment transport, coastal engineering, structural design, geotechnical design, mechanical design, electrical design, architectural design, naval architecture, project management, building and civil information modeling (BIM/CIM), and CAD drafting. Engineering Support During Advertisement (EDA): Preparing amendments to the advertised plans and specifications and updating the BIM/CIM as warranted by comments received from prospective bidders. Engineering Support During Construction (EDC): Attending pre-construction conferences; responding to contractor requests for information (RFIs) and clarifications; reviewing submittals from the construction contractor; and performing monthly or bi-weekly site visits (or visits at critical times) to witness construction practices, observe site conditions, and document implementation of the design from the designer's perspective. Levee Safety & Structural Periodic Inspections: Performing detailed, systematic technical inspections and evaluations of the safety, stability, and operational adequacy of levees and civil works structures. Support Services: Surveying and the use of aerial mapping are required to support this work. (b) Required Disciplines & Professional Qualifications: The assembled team must demonstrate professional qualifications, education, training, licensing, certification, professional registration, overall relevant experience, and longevity within their disciplines and firm. Key design personnel must include: Engineering: Structural, Civil, Hydraulic (including hydrologic analysis, sediment transport, and coastal engineering), Geotechnical, Mechanical, Electrical, Corrosion, Environmental, and Cost Engineering. Scientific & Applied Fields: Hydrologists, Geologists, Architects, Naval Architects, and Surveyors. Geospatial & Technology Specialties: Geospatial Information Systems (GIS) Mapping and Analysis, Drafting via Computer-Aided Design (Autodesk), 3D Modeling CAD consisting of Building Information Modeling (BIM), and Civil Information Modeling (CIM), and professional Project Management. (c) Types of Features & Project Scopes The work may involve existing and new projects at any design stage, involving new or existing structures, including: Hydraulic Structures: Locks, floodgates, floodwalls, levees, navigation structures, drainage canals and structures, pumping stations, and prestressed/post-tensioned concrete structures. Marine Structures: Bulkheads, dolphins, fenders, guide walls, jetties, or shoreline protection. Highway & Infrastructure Work: Roads, ramps, bridges, utility relocations, and buildings (such as warehouses, pump houses, or offices related to the structures above). Risk Reduction & Environmental Projects: Flood risk management, hurricane and storm damage risk reduction projects, non-structural techniques (including elevation), freshwater and sediment diversion projects, environmental infrastructure projects, and other multi-purpose projects. (d) Specialized Civil, Structural, Geotechnical, & Surveying Tasks: The work may involve the following detailed types of related analysis, modeling, and field work: Modeling & Structural Analysis: 3D modeling of buildings, structures, sites, and horizontal construction features; civil/site work design; structural design; planning; program and project management; finite element modeling; frame analysis; pile group analysis; and drainage analysis. Contract Package Development: Development of plans and specifications, Design-Build Requests for Proposals (RFPs), and real estate rights-of-way (ROW) drawings. Field Investigations & Testing: Hazard Toxic Radioactive Waste (HTRW) investigations; architectural treatments; landscaping; performing soil borings and soil testing to determine soil properties; and providing boring logs in accordance with USACE New Orleans District geotechnical criteria. Analytical Calculations & Engineering Evaluations: Developing pile capacity curves; bearing capacity analysis; cantilever retaining or floodwall analysis; temporary retaining structure design; time-settlement projections with lift schedules; soil pressures; seepage and dewatering analysis; stability analysis for levees using Spencer's Method and/or Janbu�s Method (including reinforced embankments, dikes, and other earthen structures); bank stability analysis; slope stability analysis for revetments, channels, and excavations; stability analysis of floodwalls (T-walls, I-walls, L-walls); downdrag and settlement analysis; numerical model

title: B21 Low Observable/Radio Frequency Hangar (LO/RF) - OT Feasibility & Business Feedback
description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought (RFI) - B-21 Low Observable / Radio Frequency Hangar DISCLAIMER. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), a Request for Qualifications (RFQ), or a commitment by the Government to write, issue, or award an agreement or contract. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. All response costs will be borne solely by the interested party. PURPOSE. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. ACQUISITION STRATEGY & NON-FAR MODEL. Statutory Authority: This project will potentially be executed as a Progressive Design-Build (PDB), Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) or Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) project utilizing Other Transaction Authority (OTA) pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Non-FAR Environment: Prospective partners are advised that the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) does NOT apply to this procurement. The negotiated, bilateral Other Transaction Agreement will serve as the sole governing contract. Standard FAR clauses are inapplicable, though federal statutory constraints (such as federal fiscal law, criminal statutes, and general civil laws) remain fully applicable. Agreement Mechanics: PBD Procurement Process: Phase 1, Design & Pre-Construction Services, a design-builder will be selected through a qualifications-based selection (QBS) process. The government will then negotiate a fee for Phase 1 services. There is no requirement to submit price proposals or design concepts during the initial selection. Phase 2, Final Design & Construction, is executed via a bilateral modification to the OT Agreement upon successful negotiation of a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) at approximately 65% design maturity. The Agreement contains an "off-ramp" clause allowing the Government to retain the design and procure construction separately if GMP negotiations fail. DBtB Procurement Process: Solicitation and evaluation during Phase 1 focuses on the qualifications, past performance, and integrated Design-Build experience of each offeror. The Government is evaluating the team and not necessarily how the offeror will design the structure. The Phase 1 evaluation results in the selection of three of the most highly qualified, competitive teams to proceed to Phase 2. Phase 2, the Government will issue the final RFP exclusively to the down-selected teams. This RFP includes the validated, performance-based requirements, establishes the firm Construction Cost Limit (CCL), and clearly defines the basic scope. Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) Procurement Process: Early involvement, separate contracts, guaranteed maximum price and collaborative delivery. PROJECT OVERVIEW & SCOPE. Title: B-21 Low Observable / Radio Frequency Hangar Location: Dyess Air Force Base, Texas Scope: Construct a new 95,529 sq. ft. Low Observable Corrosion Control Hangar (LO) and a Radio Frequency Facility (RF) for the new B-21 weapons system. The project demands a highly collaborative and iterative design process to manage complexity and a critical schedule. Target Price Range (TPR): The Government has established The Government's Target Price Estimate for construction is between $280,000,000 and $300,000,000. Projected Award Date: The Government targets the formal award of the Agreement Phase 1 (Design and Preconstruction Services) on or about July 2027. Current Design is at 100%. The Government is willing to revert to a 35% design, allowing the awardee and designer the ability to collaborate during an OTA procurement process. Period of Performance (POP): The projected construction timeline is approximately 1217 calendar days following the execution of the Phase 2 Construction modification. Product Service Code (PSC): Y1BG (Construction of Electronic and Communications Facilities). NAICS Code: 236220 (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction). INNOVATIVE METHODOLOGIES & FEEDBACK AREAS. In accordance with Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC) Design Instruction #3, the Government is seeking commercial industry feedback regarding the feasibility and market capacity for the following innovative methods: Modular and Off-Site Prefabrication: Fabricating large sections of the facility or complex mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems in factory-controlled environments to compress the construction schedule. 3D Printing: Utilizing large-scale 3D printing for secondary building components, non-load-bearing walls, or perimeter security fencing. Advanced Materials: Incorporating self-healing concrete to reduce lifecycle maintenance and maximize structural integrity, or utilizing high-performance insulation (e.g., aerogels or vacuum-insulated panels) to meet high-performance building standards. Submissions: Submit your capabilities statement and Market Intelligence response (attachment) via email toThomas Howard at Thomas.W.Howard@usace.army.mil and Nicholas Johnston at Nicholas.I.Johnston@usace.army.mil no later than Wednesday, September 23st, 2026 at 2:00 PM CDT (21:00 UTC). Use email subject: "Sources Sought Response: B21 Low Observable/Radio Frequency Hangar (LO/RF) Market Intel - [Your Firm Name]". File Naming Convention: Market Intel_B21 LO/RF_[FIRM NAME]

title: Labeling Pilot for FDF Country of Origin, API Country of Origin, and KSM Country of Origin for Pharmaceutical Products
description: 1. Purpose The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support Medical Supply Chain is conducting market research to identify U.S. or international pharmaceutical manufacturers that are willing to participate in a labeling pilot program. The pilot seeks to explore voluntary inclusion of additional product labeling data for Pharmaceutical Products identifying: Country of origin for the Finished Dose Form (FDF) Country of origin for each Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) Country of origin for each Key starting material (KSM) necessary for the production of each API Given the amount of information requested, inclusion of a QR code or link to additional information, or other methods of making the information accessible, could be considered If the country of origin of the API or KSM can vary by lot produced, DLA would be interested in the information specific to the labeled lot and to any previously produced lots This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, and responses do not commit the Government to any future acquisition or requirement. 2. Background DLA Troop Support Medical is evaluating methods to improve supply chain transparency, enhance traceability, and strengthen operational readiness by increasing visibility into the sourcing of pharmaceutical ingredients. Understanding FDF, API, and KSM origins helps support contingency planning, risk modeling, and alignment with emerging regulatory and strategic sourcing initiatives. The agency is exploring the feasibility of obtaining this information directly from manufacturers through voluntary labeling enhancements on packaging, shipping containers, or supplemental documentation. 3. Scope of Pilot The proposed labeling pilot will focus on a selected subset of generic pharmaceutical products purchased by DLA Troop Support Medical. Participating manufacturers may be asked to provide: API country of manufacture API country of origin (if different) Country of origin for the Finished Dose Form (FDF) Country of origin for each Key starting material (KSM) necessary for the production of each API If the country of origin of the API or KSM can vary by lot produced, DLA would be interested in the information specific to the labeled lot and to any previously produced lots Placement of this information on external packaging, product containers, or accompanying supply chain documentation Given the amount of information requested, inclusion of a QR code or link to additional information, or other methods of making the information accessible, could be considered Estimated production or administrative impact associated with adding these data elements DLA seeks to understand both operational feasibility and industry readiness. 4. Requested Information from Respondents Interested manufacturers are invited to submit a written response addressing the following: A. Company name, CAGE code, point of contact information B. Description of the pharmaceutical products you manufacture that are supplied or could be supplied to DLA C. Willingness to participate in a voluntary labeling or data?sharing pilot to include: Development of a labeling construct that contains all relevant sourcing information as outlined below. Obtaining approval of the labeling construct from the Food and Drug Administration. Producing labels with all required sourcing information and affixing them to products sold to the Department of War. D. Ability to provide the following information for each lot produced: API country of manufacture API country of origin (if different) Country of origin for the Finished Dose Form (FDF) Country of origin for each Key starting material (KSM) necessary for the production of each API If the country of origin of the API or KSM can vary by lot produced, DLA would be interested in the information specific to the labeled lot and to any previously produced lots Placement of this information on external packaging, product containers, or accompanying supply chain documentation Given the amount of information requested, inclusion of a QR code or link to additional information, or other methods of making the information accessible, could be considered Estimated production or administrative impact associated with adding these data elements E. Existing internal capabilities or systems that support API and KSM traceability and documentation F. Expected timeline and level of effort required to implement labeling modifications G. Any concerns, limitations, or cost impacts associated with participation H. Recommendations for structuring or scaling the pilot program 5. Submission Instructions Responses should be submitted via email in PDF or Word format to the DLA Troop Support Medical Supply Chain point of contact: Contracting Officer: Charles T. Reimer DLA Troop Support � Medical Supply Chain Email: Charles.Reimer@dla.mil Phone: 267-251-9370 (Cell)

title: RFI-AMSS Integrator
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: Arctic Mobility Sustainment System Integration IMPORTANT NOTICE The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) notice is to conduct market research to determine the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of potential business or government sources to perform system integration, kitting, packaging, and distribution for the Arctic Mobility Sustainment System (AMSS). This RFI does not constitute an Invitation for Bid (IFB), a Request for Proposal (RFP), a Request for Quote (RFQ) or an indication that the Government will contract for any of the items and/or services contained in this notice. This is not a request for proposals. No solicitation documents exist at this time. Any information provided does not constitute a proposal but will be considered an exchange of capabilities and ideas. The Government will not be responsible for any costs incurred in furnishing this information or potential participation in the event. This RFI does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise, that the Government will take procurement action in this matter. All information received in response to this notice that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. Responses will be reviewed, and businesses of interest will be contacted. Additional information may be requested. The due date for responses is 23 SEP 2026. BACKGROUND & SCOPE The Arctic Mobility Sustainment System is the successor to the legacy Ahkio system. AMSS addresses the need for equipment to operate effectively in the Arctic environment, where the extreme cold, challenging terrain, and long distances require specialized capabilities. AMSS is being developed as a system that enables dismounted Soldiers to transport sustainment and survivability equipment essential for up to 72 hours. AMSS consists of an Arctic Transport (sled), Arctic Shelter, Arctic Heater, and related Component of End Items (COEI), and will have both a Team (5-man) and a Squad (10-man) configuration. Product Manager Force Sustainment Systems (PdM FSS) is evaluating industry and/or government capabilities to serve as a Lead System Integrator (LSI) to execute procurement, quality control, packaging, kitting, and final delivery of complete systems to designated CONUS and OCONUS end users. SEE ATTACHMENT For Component of End items (COEI) - Squad configuration & KITTING, PACKAGING, AND LOGISTICS STANDARDS Information requested from RESPONDENTS Please submit a white paper addressing the below listed information of interest. The white paper and any pertinent supplemental information must not exceed a combined length of 10 pages. Please structure your response according to the sections below. Do not attach marketing brochures, test reports, or other extraneous materials to your submission, as they will not be reviewed nor will they be considered as part of the evaluation. Electronic copies of responses should be in PDF format using size 12 font with one-inch margins. Following a review of the responses, PdM FSS may request additional information from respondents about their proposed capabilities. **For Arsenals and Depot respondents**: In addition to addressing each section below, please provide overarching acquisition strategy to include: Procurement Contracting Experience and Capability Describe overall integration capabilities, and any relevant experience conducting integration, kitting, and packaging efforts in support of the U.S. Government. For such cases, provide data on production capacity, time needed to ramp up production capacity, and throughput per month. Any available production metrics are welcomed. Provide CAGE code and SAM.gov active registration status. Integration Strategy Packaging Blueprints � Provide a packaging blueprint (one for Squad, one for Team) that adheres to the standards provided. Please include details of quality control and compliance with Government standards. Procurement � Describe strategy for procuring all COEI items, kit assembly and packaging, and shipment. Please address the following cost-saving opportunities in your response: Volume Discounting � Describe how your company will structure purchasing agreements with OEMs to capture maximum volume discounts. Long Lead Item Management � Identify which COEI components represent the highest cost and longest lead times. Propose strategies to mitigate price volatility and inflation. Kitting and Packaging Labor Efficiencies � Detail any packaging design options (such as custom-molded inserts, modular tool rolls, or nested component layouts) that would reduce the physical labor hours required to assemble, inspect, and verify each kit. Identify which items are best suited to remain in their original OEM packaging versus those requiring complete repackaging under MIL-STD-2073-1. Logistical & Freight Consolidation Strategies � Propose packaging arrangements inside or alongside the Arctic Transport (sled) that minimizes the overall cubic volume (cube) of the shipped kit, maximizing the number of units that can fit on a standard 463L military pallet or inside a standard ISO shipping container. Based on your established logistical footprint, propose optimal staging, warehousing, or transit nodes to minimize freight costs and transit risks when shipping to final destinations in NORTHCOM (Alaska (OCONUS) and lower 48 (CONUS) locations), PACOM (1st Special Forces Group in Japan), and EUCOM (10th Special Forces Group in Germany). Warehousing, Storage, and Facilities Strategies � Provide location(s) where the integration and packaging effort will be performed. Provide information on storage, available floor space, and on-site physical security. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) Cost Estimate Assuming a destination of Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska, identify logistics, staging, packaging and freight costs for the shipment of: 2,000 AMSS Squad Kits Assume a COEI procurement cost of $25,000 per unit. 1,000 AMSS Team Kits Assume a COEI procurement cost of $20,000 per unit. Risk Identification and Mitigation Identify potential risks in the following areas and propose a mitigation strategy for each: Supply Chain Risk � NDAA Section 889 compliance, long product lead times, and price volatility. Integration Risk � Ensuring kit accuracy and quality assurance. Logistics Risk � Physical security of system items at integration facility, shipping to remote locations, and transportation damage (including sharp items damaging other items inside packaging). Point of Contact Provide name, email, and phone number for company representative(s). The Government team will contact respondents if there is continued interest. The Government team reserves the right to request additional information from all respondents. SUBMISSION DATE AND ADDRESS Electronic responses to this notice are requested to be emailed to the following Points of Contact: Raul Lopez, Project Lead, raul.a.lopez.civ@army.mil Clinton McAdams, Project Engineer, clinton.b.mcadams.civ@army.mil The subject line of the e-mail should contain the words �RFI Response - Arctic Mobility Sustainment System (AMSS) Integration�. Please note: Brochures or other descriptions of general organizational or individual capabilities will not be accepted as a response. All responses will be given an identification number, and an email will acknowledge receipt. NOTE: This RFI does not indicate that the Government will contract for any of the items and/or services contained in this notice. All information received in response to this notice that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. Responses may not include classified material. Responses to this notice will not be returned. No reimbursement will be made for any costs to provide information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. title: Germany – Engineering design services – Gemeinde Dümmer - Umbau und Sanierung der Kita Seepferdchen
description: Die Gemeinde Dümmer beabsichtigt aufgrund demografischer Veränderungen und bestehender baulicher und brandschutztechnischer Mängel den Umbau und die Sanierung der bestehenden Kindertagesstätte „Seepferdchen“. Derzeit werden alle drei Geschosse des Vorderhauses, ein Teil des hofseitigen Gebäudes und der neue Verbinder von der KITA genutzt. Ein weiterer Teil des hofseitigen Gebäudes wird durch die Gemeinde genutzt. Diese Nutzung soll zukünftig entfallen und der Gebäudeanteil dann der KITA zugeordnet werden. Die geplante Kindertagesstätte ist für die Betreuung von 55 Kindern ausgelegt. Die Zusammenstellung der einzelnen Bereiche stellt sich dabei wie folgt dar: - 10 Krippenkinder - 45 Kindergartenkinder, davon jeweils 3 Gruppen mit je 15 Kindern Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung ist die Objektplanung Gebäude gem. HOAI 2021 Teil 3 Objektplanung, Abschnitt 1 Gebäude und Innenräume, Leistungsphasen 2-8. Die Beauftragung der Stufe 1 (LPH 1-4) erfolgt sofort, die Beauftragung der Stufe 2 (LPH 5-8) erfolgt nach Bewilligung von Fördermitteln. Ein Anspruch des Auftragnehmers auf die Beauftragung der Stufe 2 besteht nicht.
